topic: AI Coding Agent Capability Matrix 2026: MCP, HTTP Transport, Rules, Hooks, and Sandboxes Compared

competitors.title: Best AI Coding Agents in 2026: Harness, Cost, and Accuracy Compared
key_points: Frames the 2026 market around harness depth, remote or async execution, token cost, and benchmark accuracy rather than raw model quality alone.
Compares Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Devin, Aider, and Replit Agent as distinct workflow categories.
Useful competitor angle: frontier models are converging, so the surrounding agent harness is now the practical differentiator.

Can inform the security section but should be backed by official Claude Code docs for exact product behavior.

competitors.title: Claude Code Sandbox Analysis Report
key_points: Breaks Claude Code attack surfaces into bash commands, file access, network access, MCP servers, hooks and plugins, API keys, telemetry, and session data.
Useful for emphasizing that MCP, hooks, and sandbox controls are security surfaces, not just extensibility features.
Supports a practical checklist format for teams evaluating agent risk.

competitors.title: Critical Cursor Flaws Could Let Prompt Injection Escape Sandbox and Run Commands
key_points: Reports CVE-2026-50548 and CVE-2026-50549, patched in Cursor 3.0, involving prompt injection and sandbox escape.
Useful news hook for why sandbox implementation details matter in AI coding agent comparisons.
Use carefully: this is a security news source, not Cursor's official documentation.
Codex supports STDIO and Streamable HTTP MCP servers in CLI and IDE extension, with bearer token and OAuth support for HTTP servers.
Codex uses AGENTS.md for durable repo guidance, skills for reusable workflows, MCP for external tools, hooks for lifecycle automation, and rules for command policy.
Codex sandboxing separates technical boundaries from approval policy; local CLI and IDE use OS-level sandboxing, while cloud tasks run in isolated managed containers.
Claude Code has managed, user, project, and local configuration scopes.
Project scope is designed for team-shared settings including permissions, hooks, MCP servers, plugins, and standardized tooling.
Claude Code uses CLAUDE.md and related memory files for persistent instructions and context.
Claude Code hooks can be shell commands, HTTP endpoints, LLM prompts, or MCP tool hooks.
Hook events include session, prompt, tool-call, permission, subagent, task, file, config, compaction, and MCP elicitation lifecycle points.
PreToolUse hooks can block tool calls, making hooks a deterministic policy layer when configured correctly.
Claude Code connects to external tools through MCP and supports project and user level configuration.
MCP is a major extension surface for Claude Code, but it needs allowlists and managed settings for enterprise control.
Repository administrators can configure MCP servers for Copilot cloud agent and Copilot code review.
GitHub notes that Copilot cloud agent and Copilot code review currently support MCP tools, not MCP resources or prompts.
Once configured, Copilot can use available MCP tools autonomously without asking approval for each tool use.
Copilot cloud agent includes default GitHub and Playwright MCP servers.
The default GitHub MCP server uses a specially scoped token with read-only access to the current repository unless customized.
The default Playwright MCP server is constrained to web resources hosted inside Copilot's own environment.
Copilot cloud agent exposes repository and organization level firewall controls.
Repository administrators can enable or disable the integrated firewall, recommended allowlist, and custom allowlist rules depending on organization policy.
Firewall configuration is a key differentiator from local-only agents because it governs hosted agent egress.
Copilot CLI can run sessions inside a local sandbox that restricts filesystem, network, and system capabilities.
The CLI exposes slash commands for settings and sandbox mode management.
Windsurf Cascade supports MCP with stdio, HTTP, and SSE transports.
Teams and Enterprise plans expose admin controls for MCP use.
MCP can be configured through settings, marketplace flow, or raw mcp_config.json.
Gemini CLI MCP supports Stdio, SSE, and Streamable HTTP transports.
Gemini CLI discovers MCP tools, prompts, and resources and allows resources to be referenced with @ syntax.
The documentation states unpaid tier and Google One users are being moved from Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI on June 18, 2026, which should be mentioned as an availability caveat.
Cline rules are Markdown files for persistent coding standards and instructions across conversations.
Cline is strong for open-source, user-controlled agent workflows but typically relies on user-configured approvals and external sandboxing rather than a single managed enterprise sandbox story.
Continue supports MCP setup through its configuration system.
Continue's positioning is strongest for open-source customization, BYO models, and team workflows rather than proprietary hosted autonomy.
VS Code supports MCP server configuration and can enable sandboxing for local MCP servers with filesystem and network rules.
This is relevant because GitHub Copilot's IDE surface inherits much of the VS Code agent customization ecosystem.

stats.fact: Codex supports both STDIO and Streamable HTTP MCP servers, including bearer token and OAuth authentication for HTTP servers.
Codex defaults to network-off local workspace-write behavior, with OS-level sandbox enforcement locally and isolated managed containers in Codex cloud.
Claude Code project scope is explicitly intended for team-shared settings such as permissions, hooks, MCP servers, plugins, and standardized tooling.
Claude Code hook events cover session, prompt, tool, permission, subagent, task, config, file, worktree, compaction, and MCP elicitation lifecycle points.
GitHub Copilot cloud agent and Copilot code review currently support MCP tools, but not MCP resources or prompts.
GitHub's default cloud-agent MCP setup includes GitHub and Playwright MCP servers with scoped access behavior.
GitHub Copilot cloud agent exposes repository and organization level firewall configuration including recommended and custom allowlists.
Windsurf Cascade MCP supports stdio, HTTP, and SSE transports.
Gemini CLI MCP supports Stdio, SSE, and Streamable HTTP transports and discovers tools, resources, and prompts.
Gemini CLI docs state unpaid tier and Google One users will be replaced by Antigravity CLI on June 18, 2026.
Cline rules are Markdown files for persistent instructions and coding standards across conversations.
The Hacker News reported two Cursor sandbox escape CVEs in July 2026, patched in Cursor 3.0, illustrating why version-specific sandbox claims matter.

angles: The new buying criterion is harness depth: MCP, hooks, rules, sandboxes, approval flows, and network policy now matter as much as model benchmark scores.
MCP support is not binary. Compare transports, authentication, resources/prompts support, approval behavior, tool allowlists, and admin controls.
Rules guide, hooks enforce: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursor/rules, and .clinerules shape model behavior, while lifecycle hooks and sandbox policy create deterministic guardrails.
Cloud agents and local agents have different trust boundaries: Copilot and Codex cloud can isolate hosted work, while local tools must protect the developer machine directly.
Streamable HTTP is becoming the dividing line for modern MCP: Codex, Windsurf, and Gemini CLI document it clearly, while some tools require closer version-by-version verification.
The security section should avoid generic claims like 'sandboxed' and ask: sandboxed from what, enforced by whom, with what filesystem and network defaults?
Enterprise evaluation should include managed settings, MCP allowlists, hook trust, network egress controls, secrets scoping, and auditability.
Open-source agents win on transparency and model freedom, but closed platforms often win on integrated policy, hosted environments, and admin controls.
Cursor's security news hook is valuable for timeliness, but the article should be precise: patched versions and exact CVEs matter more than broad fear framing.
Gemini CLI requires an availability footnote because current docs warn that unpaid tier and Google One users are moving to Antigravity CLI.

recommended_structure.intro: Start with the thesis that model quality has converged enough that harness capability is now the practical differentiator.
verdicts: Best overall policy-rich stack: OpenAI Codex
Best lifecycle hooks and terminal depth: Claude Code
Best GitHub-native enterprise workflow: GitHub Copilot
Best broad MCP transport in an IDE: Windsurf

risk_box: Do not trust 'supports MCP' without checking transport, auth, resources/prompts, tool approvals, and admin allowlists.
Do not trust 'sandboxed' without checking filesystem writes, network defaults, local/private network rules, and escape patch status.
Instruction files are not enforcement. Pair them with hooks, tests, linters, sandbox policy, and CI.
